pathway.title: Versant Media Group, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The strongest support is low leverage backed by cash flow that still covers debt service by a wide margin. Total debt is 1.37x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and net debt of USD 1,876 million is 0.88x, or USD 1,976 million and 0.92x pro forma for the USD 100 million accelerated repurchase from 2026-11-04; reported EBITDA covered nine-month cash interest 11.25x, and free cash flow of USD 1,640 million over twelve months converts 76.60% of EBITDA and is 56.03% of total debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

- The weakest dimension is revenue durability, because the two lines that earn 82.40% of revenue are in measured decline. Linear distribution fell 6.49% and advertising 3.56% in nine months 2026, after subscriber declines of 8% in each of 2024 and 2025 and a ratings decline of 17% at the networks in 2025, while platforms grew 6.43% but by only USD 40 million against a USD 201 million fall in linear distribution; issuer-stated Adjusted EBITDA fell 10.96% in nine months, and its last-twelve-month margin of 33.94% is 2.32 percentage points below FY2025. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-11

- Operating leverage is high because content costs are fixed and larger than the debt. Programming and production obligations of USD 5,726 million, mostly multiyear sports rights, are 1.96x total debt and 2.67x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, and programming and production costs are 36.10% of last-twelve-month revenue, so lost revenue falls almost fully into EBITDA until rights expire, the earliest being the 2027-28 season. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CALC-10

- Financial policy is the swing factor and is drawing the cushion down. In nine months 2026 distributions of USD 406 million and acquisitions and investments of USD 806 million together took 100.17% of free cash flow of USD 1,210 million, net debt rose USD 400 million in the third quarter, and the USD 2,250 million separation payment to Comcast, 75.00% of the debt principal raised, set the starting leverage. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-18

- Liquidity and refinancing are adequate and concentrated in one date. Cash plus the undrawn USD 750 million revolving facility is USD 1,801 million before the announced repurchase, for which pro forma cash is not established, and it covers the USD 120 million of annual amortization 15.01x; every instrument matures in January 2031, so refinancing depends on 2030 earnings and market access then, not on a nearer wall. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99–100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-07

- The primary downside path is a faster fall in linear distribution and advertising against fixed content costs while discretionary cash use continues. If the nine-month declines repeated for twelve months with costs unchanged, reported EBITDA would fall USD 251.46 million to USD 1,889.54 million and pro forma net leverage would reach 1.05x; if the declines in linear distribution and advertising doubled, EBITDA would fall USD 558.60 million to USD 1,582.40 million, pro forma net leverage would reach 1.25x, cover on accrued interest would be 7.46x, and distributions and acquisitions at the nine-month pace would draw cash down by USD 534.60 million in a year. That is erosion of the cushion, not a liquidity event, and the first signals are linear distribution declines above 6.49% and an Adjusted EBITDA margin below 34.13%. Basis: calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-11

- Control and governance add event risk without adding support. One Class B holder holds a third of the votes with separate approval rights, a tax matters agreement restricts equity issuance for two years after 2026-01-02 so an equity cure is not a realistic backstop, and the sponsor and governance risk level assessed in Business & governance is medium. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- The covenant and the asset base are the least visible parts of the credit. The maximum first lien net leverage of 3.50x is tested from the third quarter of 2026 on a definition that is not supplied, and goodwill of USD 8,127 million is 64.21% of total assets with fair value only about 11% above carrying value at the networks reporting unit, so neither covenant headroom nor impairment room is established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-19

runs.text: Cash flow covers debt service by a wide margin, which is the main support for creditors. Free cash flow of USD 1,640 million over twelve months is 56.03% of total debt and, with capital expenditures at 2.09% of revenue, most EBITDA reaches cash; scheduled amortization of USD 120 million a year is 7.32% of that free cash flow, so scheduled debt service would stay covered even if free cash flow fell sharply. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-21

Liquidity and a single maturity date remove near-term refinancing risk. Cash plus the undrawn USD 750 million revolving facility is USD 1,801 million before the announced repurchase and all debt falls due in January 2031, so default risk in the next two years rests on discretionary choices, not on a maturity. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99–100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation CALC-07

Brand reach and a growing platforms line give some revenue outside cable fees. The networks reach 49 million to 60 million households each, sports rights run into the 2030s, and platforms revenue grew 6.43% to 13.44% of nine-month revenue, although management's description of audience strength is not tested against peers. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01

Revenue is structurally declining in its two largest lines and costs do not fall with it. Linear distribution and advertising are 82.40% of revenue and fell 6.49% and 3.56%, while content obligations of USD 5,726 million are 1.96x total debt, so each lost dollar of revenue is mostly a lost dollar of EBITDA until rights expire. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-10

Financial policy is spending the cushion: distributions of USD 406 million and acquisitions and investments of USD 806 million took 100.17% of free cash flow in nine months, net debt rose USD 400 million in the third quarter, and a further USD 100 million repurchase was announced, so deleveraging is not being chosen while earnings fall. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-09

Dependence on Comcast and a concentrated control structure limit creditors' options. Advertising, 23.63% of nine-month revenue, is sold by NBCUniversal for approximately two years, the CNBC trademark licence has a five-year initial term, a Class B holder has a third of the votes, and equity issuance is restricted until early 2028, so there is neither a stated support provider nor a ready equity cure. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Asset quality and covenant visibility are weak points. Goodwill is 64.21% of total assets, the networks reporting unit's fair value is only about 11% above carrying value, and the 3.50x first lien covenant cannot be tested because its definition is not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation CALC-19

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Versant separated from Comcast on 2026-01-02 when Comcast distributed 100% of the Class A and Class B shares to its shareholders at one Versant share for every 25 Comcast shares, and the Class A shares began trading on 2026-01-05. Before that date Versant was a wholly owned Comcast subsidiary and its statements are combined carve-out figures. Agreements with Comcast cover separation and distribution, tax matters, transition services, employee matters, intellectual property licences and commercial arrangements. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108

The separation was financed with USD 3,000 million of secured debt: USD 1,000 million of senior secured notes due January 2031, issued in October 2025 with proceeds held in escrow until the separation; a USD 1,000 million Term Loan A and a USD 750 million revolving facility under a credit agreement dated 2025-10-03; and a USD 1,000 million Term Loan B under a credit agreement dated 2026-01-02. Term Loan A was drawn on 2026-01-02 and the revolving facility is undrawn. USD 2,250 million of the proceeds was paid in cash to Comcast as consideration for assets contributed, which is 75.00% of the principal raised. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99–101; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; calculation CALC-13

Term Loan A amortizes at 5.00% a year and Term Loan B at 7.00% a year in quarterly instalments from 2026-09-30; Term Loan A bears SOFR plus 1.75%, Term Loan B SOFR plus 3.50%, and the revolving facility carries a 0.25% commitment fee. The notes may be redeemed at par plus a make-whole premium before 2028-01-30 and carry customary limits on additional debt, liens, restricted payments and affiliate transactions. Term Loan A and the revolving facility carry a maximum consolidated first lien net leverage ratio of 3.50x from the third quarter of 2026, defined in an agreement that is not supplied, and the company reported compliance at 2026-09-30. Interest rate swaps of USD 975 million notional entered in March 2026 leave about 66% of debt principal at fixed rates. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99–102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation CALC-20

After the separation the company bought Full Swing for USD 536 million in cash on 2026-08-03, acquired other businesses for aggregate consideration of USD 215 million in the first half, sold SportsEngine in the second quarter for an aggregate USD 143 million, and returned USD 406 million to shareholders in nine months. The board declared a fourth-quarter dividend payable on 2027-01-25, and an accelerated repurchase of USD 100 million was announced to start on 2026-11-04; the filings do not confirm that it has started. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt rose from USD 983 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 2,927 million at 2026-09-30 because the two USD 1,000 million term loans were drawn on 2026-01-02, so total debt to reported EBITDA moved from 0.43x on the year-end notes alone to 1.32x at 2026-03-31 and 1.37x at 2026-09-30. The rise is set by the financing, not by earnings: last-twelve-month reported EBITDA fell from USD 2,282 million for FY2025 to USD 2,141 million, so each further acquisition or buyback adds to net debt without an earnings cushion. In the third quarter cash fell by USD 427 million while total debt fell by USD 27 million, so net debt rose by USD 400 million to USD 1,876 million; the nine-month cash flow statement shows USD 696 million spent on acquisitions, USD 300 million on repurchases and USD 106 million on dividends.

Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 22.52x for three months, 21.34x for six months and 11.25x for nine months, so the nine-month figure is the better guide to run-rate cover and the earlier ratios flatter it.

fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 1,313 million for nine months 2026 against USD 1,546 million a year earlier, a fall of USD 233 million; receivables absorbed USD 392 million in 2026 against an inflow of USD 48 million in 2025, which the company attributes mainly to Comcast retaining advertising sales receivables after the separation, so 2026 operating cash flow is understated against a normal year. Capital expenditures of USD 103 million left free cash flow of USD 1,210 million for nine months against USD 1,425 million, before acquisitions, buybacks and dividends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of USD 1,051 million and the undrawn USD 750 million revolver give USD 1,801 million of liquidity at 2026-09-30, against scheduled term loan amortization of USD 30 million for the rest of 2026 and USD 120 million a year to 2030, so near-term repayment is not the constraint; the first large maturity is the 2031 amount of USD 2,460 million, which includes the USD 1,000 million notes. The binding use of liquidity is discretionary: the company repurchased USD 300 million of stock and paid USD 106 million of dividends in nine months and announced a further USD 100 million accelerated repurchase from 2026-11-04. No letters of credit drawn on the revolver are stated in any source, and the revolver's availability at 2025-12-31 is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 3,060 million in FY2023 to USD 2,837 million in FY2024 and USD 2,425 million in FY2025, and was USD 1,681 million for nine months 2026 against USD 1,888 million a year earlier, a fall of USD 207 million; third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was USD 353 million against USD 445 million, a fall of USD 92 million. Linear distribution revenue fell to USD 2,894 million for nine months from USD 3,095 million and advertising revenue to USD 1,164 million from USD 1,207 million, only partly offset by platforms revenue of USD 662 million against USD 622 million, so the shrinking pay-television networks are not yet replaced by digital platforms. Subscribers to multichannel video providers fell 8% in each of 2024 and 2025, and programming and production obligations of USD 5,726 million are fixed, so continued subscriber declines compress EBITDA faster than costs can fall.

Operating lease commitments are also outside debt, including USD 243 million of future minimum payments on the New York office lease net of lease incentives.

fields.value: Net debt of USD 1,876 million is before the announced USD 100 million accelerated repurchase from 2026-11-04, which would bring it to USD 1,976 million, or 0.92x; the dividend paid on 2026-10-22 and the one payable on 2027-01-25 are excluded because the sources state only USD 0.375 per share. These events fall after the balance sheet date and are not blended into any period figure.

fields.value: The 2025 comparatives are carve-out statements with costs allocated by Comcast, so every last-twelve-month figure here mixes a combined 2025 stub with standalone 2026 periods. Reported EBITDA is calculated because the issuer prints only an adjusted figure; the adjustments were USD 142 million in FY2025 and USD 5 million for nine months 2026, so the two measures converge as separation costs end. The filings' own rounding leaves four cash flow totals that cannot be supported by the other printed totals, written as not supplied, and the covenant measure cannot be compared with any ratio here because its definition is not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement is not supplied and the first lien net leverage covenant of 3.50:1.00 is defined only there, so no covenant headroom is stated and none is inferred. Severity is Medium. Supplying the credit and guaranty agreements would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The statements for FY2023 to FY2025 and every 2025 interim comparative are combined carve-out figures with costs allocated by Comcast, so trends across the separation, and the 2025 stub inside each last-twelve-month figure, are not like for like. Severity is Medium. No stand-alone pro forma figures are printed, so the sources cannot close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No source states the lien ranking of the term loans or the revolver against the notes, so the debt stack shows only the notes and the three credit facilities are left out of it. Severity is Medium. The indenture, the credit agreements and any intercreditor agreement would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings print no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated as operating income plus depreciation and amortization; the nine-month 2026 depreciation line includes a USD 39 million loss on the SportsEngine sale, which therefore sits outside EBITDA. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid and cash taxes paid are not stated for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 or the 2025 interim periods, so interest cover cannot be calculated for 2025 and cover for 2026 is on a year-to-date basis, not last twelve months. Severity is Low. A post-separation year of cash flow would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The net cash change printed for FY2024, FY2025 and 9M 2025, and the closing cash printed for FY2023, cannot be supported by the other printed totals because the filings round each total to the nearest million; they are written as not supplied, not adjusted. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings print dashes in many cells, for example interest expense before 2026, noncontrolling interests, restricted cash and several investing and financing lines; each is written as not supplied and none is read as zero. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The first-quarter 2025 operating cash flow lines add to USD 476 million against USD 478 million printed and the filing does not say why; the printed total is used. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - At 2026-09-30 the two balance sheet debt lines add to USD 2,926 million while the debt note totals USD 2,927 million, and the printed principal components add to USD 2,971 million against USD 2,970 million drawn less repaid; both differences are rounding, and the note total and the derived principal are used. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sources do not say whether the revolver could be drawn at 2025-12-31, so undrawn committed facilities at that date are not supplied, and no letter-of-credit usage or sublimit is stated for any date. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Instrument-level carrying values are not printed, only the aggregate unamortized costs of USD 43 million, so the debt instruments table carries principal and a separate financing cost adjustment; the printed principals plus that adjustment add to USD 2,928 million, one more than the printed total, through rounding. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The aggregate cost of the dividend paid on 2026-10-22 and of the dividend payable on 2027-01-25 is not stated, only USD 0.375 per share, so no pro forma figure is given for either. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The first-quarter report states total minimum lease payments of USD 286 million for the New York office lease while later reports state USD 243 million net of lease incentives; the later figure is used and the sources do not reconcile the two. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The second-quarter report states the Full Swing price as approximately USD 530 million while the third-quarter report states USD 536 million in cash paid at closing; the later figure is used. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The overview of the annual report states 2024 Adjusted EBITDA as USD 2.80 billion while its results table and reconciliation state USD 2,837 million; the reconciliation is used, as the earlier source readiness review also found, and the difference of USD 37 million is unexplained. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA bridge does not reconcile exactly because reported EBITDA of USD 2,282 million plus adjustments of USD 142 million is USD 2,424 million against USD 2,425 million printed; the bridge is drawn for nine months 2026, where the steps reconcile exactly. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, and the filings report one segment, so no segment revenue schedule exists; revenue is shown by type instead. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The quarterly reports print cumulative cash flow statements, so no discrete second-quarter or third-quarter cash flow is stated, and Q4 2025 revenue and Adjusted EBITDA are calculated from the year less nine months because no fourth quarter is reported. Severity is Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Guarantor entities and their separate financial information are not supplied, so the guarantee group cannot be measured against the consolidated figures. Severity is Low. The credit agreements and a subsidiary list would close it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance for Versant Media Group, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. The module sets out the separation and financing transaction, ownership and control, the operating model, and governance and capital-allocation behaviour from the four filings and the source readiness output. It draws no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance is a moderate credit risk: one Class B holder holds a third of the votes, and cash is going to buybacks and acquisitions while earnings fall, so creditors should rely on covenants and liquidity, not on owner support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a United States cable-network group whose largest revenue line, linear distribution at 58.76% of nine-month 2026 revenue, fell 6.49% in the period. Versant borrowed USD 3,000 million for the separation and paid USD 2,250 million of it to Comcast, then spent USD 406 million on dividends and buybacks and USD 806 million on acquisitions and investments in nine months. The executed debt documents are not supplied, so capacity to distribute more is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control sits with one Class B holder, not with a financial sponsor, which adds approval-right and transfer-of-control risk without any support commitment. The Class B shares carry a non-dilutable third of the votes and separate approval rights over mergers, equity issuances and changes to the articles even if the board and other shareholders approve, yet they are 0.28% of the shares outstanding. The annual report says the holder could transfer effective control by selling them, and no equity cure or continuing support commitment from this holder or from Comcast appears in the filings; the only payment from Comcast's side was USD 70 million at the separation, for a purpose the filings do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The separation was financed with debt that mostly left the company, so the borrowing funded a transfer to the former parent rather than the issuer's own liquidity. Of USD 3,000 million of principal raised across the notes and two term loans, USD 2,250 million, or 75.00%, was paid in cash to Comcast for the assets contributed, and the remainder of USD 750 million before costs went to general corporate purposes. All three debt instruments and the USD 750 million revolving facility are secured on substantially all assets of the company and its guarantor subsidiaries and fall due in January 2031; the first lien net leverage covenant of 3.50x applies from the third quarter of 2026 on a definition that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99–100; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation CALC-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The operating base is large but shrinking at its core, and the margin is falling. Linear distribution, 58.76% of nine-month 2026 revenue, fell 6.49% as subscriber losses outran contractual rate increases; advertising, 23.63%, fell 3.56%; platforms, 13.44%, grew 6.43% but by USD 40 million against a USD 201 million fall in linear distribution. Total revenue fell 3.01% and the issuer-stated Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 34.13% from 37.18%, a comparison that sets 2026 standalone costs against 2025 costs allocated by Comcast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Content commitments are a fixed claim larger than the debt and fall mostly beyond one year, so operating leverage rises as revenue shrinks. Programming and production obligations, mainly multiyear sports rights, total USD 5,726 million, with USD 1,402 million due within 12 months and 75.52% beyond that; the earliest major sports rights expire with the 2027-28 season and others run to 2036.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Dependence on Comcast has changed form rather than ended. NBCUniversal sells the domestic linear and related digital advertising inventory, the second-largest revenue line at 23.63% of nine-month revenue, for approximately two years; Comcast provides transition services generally for up to two years; the CNBC trademark licence has an initial term of five years; arrangements with Comcast were between 10% and 11% of revenue in each year to 2025, with related-party sales at 13.88% of 2025 revenue; and Comcast kept advertising receivables, which lowered 2026 operating cash flow. Comcast's share of revenue after the separation is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation is mixed: distributions and acquisitions are running together while earnings fall, and they are paid from cash, not new debt. In nine months 2026 the company paid USD 106 million of dividends and USD 300 million of buybacks, together 33.55% of free cash flow of USD 1,210 million, and spent USD 806 million on acquisitions and investments, so cash fell USD 427 million in the third quarter to USD 1,051 million. A further USD 100 million accelerated repurchase was announced to start on 2026-11-04, USD 700 million of authorisation remained at 2026-09-30, and the dividend runs at about USD 205.04 million a year at the current share count. The debt documents restrict dividends, buybacks and investments subject to exceptions, but the baskets are not supplied, so the only limit stated at a level is the leverage covenant.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_vsnt-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-19; calculation CALC-22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisition appetite is a 2026 pattern, small against the revenue base so far and paid from cash. Full Swing cost USD 536 million in cash on 2026-08-03, with goodwill at 60.26% of the price and USD 24 million of revenue since closing, and other businesses acquired in the first half cost aggregate consideration of USD 215 million; the annual report names Free TV Networks, bought in January 2026, without a price. The filings state that the acquisitions did not materially affect revenue or net income and give no acquired earnings, so the leverage effect of the purchases is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The tax matters agreement removes equity as a funding source until early 2028, which leaves acquisitions and any deleveraging to cash flow and debt. For two years after 2026-01-02 the company may not issue stock beyond employee safe harbours, may repurchase only through open-market purchases of less than 20% of its stock in aggregate, may not change voting rights and may not stop the active conduct of its business unless it obtains a tax ruling or opinion, and it must indemnify Comcast, without a cap, for tax losses it causes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The asset base rests on goodwill with a thin test cushion, so a lower cash-flow outlook would first show up as an impairment signal. Goodwill is 64.21% of total assets, equity less goodwill and intangibles is negative USD 462 million, the networks reporting unit holds USD 6.68 billion of goodwill, its fair value exceeded carrying value by only about 11% at the 2026-07-01 test, and a rise of 100 bp in the discount rate would cut fair value by about USD 660 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sponsor and governance risk level is medium: no creditor-adverse action is documented, but the documents that would show legal capacity are missing and the governance record is only about ten months old. Searches of the four filings found no amendment, waiver, exchange offer, priming step or fee to an owner, while the separation agreements were negotiated before the company had a board or management independent of Comcast, the annual report has no internal-control report, and the executed debt documents, the 2026 proxy statement and the separation agreements are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 110–111; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 111–113; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is liquidity and conduct to date. Cash of USD 1,051 million sits beside an undrawn USD 750 million revolving facility, scheduled repayments are only USD 30 million for the rest of 2026, the first lien covenant was met at 2026-09-30, free cash flow covered distributions 2.98x, and the filings show no amendment, waiver or priming step. The Class B holder owns 0.28% of the shares and the Class A holders, former Comcast shareholders, hold two thirds of the votes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to high risk if buybacks or acquisitions were funded with revolver borrowings or new secured debt, if the first lien covenant were amended or waived, or if the Class B holder transferred effective control; it would move to low risk if the executed credit agreements showed binding limits on restricted payments and acquisitions and the covenant headroom proved wide.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreements and indenture are not supplied, so whether restricted-payment, investment and debt baskets allow further distributions or acquisitions cannot be tested, and the medium risk level could move either way once they are read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so director independence, executive pay and any Class A holdings of the Class B holder are not established, and the control finding rests on the annual report's summary of voting rights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The separation, tax matters, transition services and employee matters agreements are not supplied, so the length, cost and caps of Comcast's services and indemnities are known only from risk-factor summaries, and the finding that equity is unavailable until early 2028 rests on that summary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Subscriber counts, carriage-agreement expiry dates, rates and revenue by network are not disclosed, so the pace of linear decline and its concentration by brand cannot be projected beyond the reported revenue lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2025 and earlier statements are combined carve-out figures with costs allocated by Comcast, so the fall in margin from nine months 2025 to nine months 2026 compares unlike cost bases and is indicative only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings of the businesses acquired in 2026 are not disclosed, so the effect of USD 806 million of acquisitions and investments on leverage and earnings cannot be established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Versant separated from Comcast on 2026-01-02 when Comcast distributed 100% of the Class A and Class B shares to its shareholders at one Versant share for every 25 Comcast shares, and the Class A shares began trading on 2026-01-05. Before that date Versant was a wholly owned Comcast subsidiary and its statements are combined carve-out figures. Agreements with Comcast cover separation and distribution, tax matters, transition services, employee matters, intellectual property licences and commercial arrangements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The separation was financed with USD 3,000 million of secured debt: USD 1,000 million of senior secured notes due January 2031, issued in October 2025 with proceeds held in escrow until the separation; a USD 1,000 million Term Loan A and a USD 750 million revolving facility under a credit agreement dated 2025-10-03; and a USD 1,000 million Term Loan B under a credit agreement dated 2026-01-02. Term Loan A was drawn on 2026-01-02 and the revolving facility is undrawn. USD 2,250 million of the proceeds was paid in cash to Comcast as consideration for assets contributed, which is 75.00% of the principal raised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99–101; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; calculation CALC-13

fields.value: Term Loan A amortizes at 5.00% a year and Term Loan B at 7.00% a year in quarterly instalments from 2026-09-30; Term Loan A bears SOFR plus 1.75%, Term Loan B SOFR plus 3.50%, and the revolving facility carries a 0.25% commitment fee. The notes may be redeemed at par plus a make-whole premium before 2028-01-30 and carry customary limits on additional debt, liens, restricted payments and affiliate transactions. Term Loan A and the revolving facility carry a maximum consolidated first lien net leverage ratio of 3.50x from the third quarter of 2026, defined in an agreement that is not supplied, and the company reported compliance at 2026-09-30. Interest rate swaps of USD 975 million notional entered in March 2026 leave about 66% of debt principal at fixed rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 1 | Erosion of linear distribution and advertising revenue | Linear distribution fell 6.49% and advertising 3.56% in nine months 2026; subscribers fell 8% in each of 2024 and 2025 and ratings fell 17% in 2025; the two lines are 82.40% of revenue; platforms grew USD 40 million against a USD 201 million fall in linear distribution | Fee revenue is paid per subscriber and advertising is priced on ratings, so both fall with cable viewing, and growth in platforms is too small to offset | Lowers EBITDA and free cash flow over the life of the debt; the main driver of default risk before the 2031 maturity | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 2 | Low leverage and strong cash conversion | Net debt USD 1,876 million, 0.88x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, and USD 1,976 million, 0.92x, pro forma for the USD 100 million accelerated repurchase from 2026-11-04; free cash flow USD 1,640 million, 76.60% of EBITDA and 56.03% of total debt; reported EBITDA covered nine-month cash interest 11.25x | Low debt against earnings and cash leaves room for earnings to fall before debt service is stressed | Supports low near-term default risk and refinancing capacity | Positive | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 3 | Liquidity and a single January 2031 maturity | Cash plus the undrawn USD 750 million revolving facility is USD 1,801 million before the announced repurchase, 15.01x the USD 120 million of annual amortization; all debt falls due in January 2031 | No maturity or large amortization before 2031 removes refinancing pressure, leaving liquidity to be consumed only by discretionary choices | Supports liquidity and defers refinancing risk to 2030 earnings and market access | Positive | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 4 | Fixed content commitments | Programming and production obligations of USD 5,726 million, USD 1,402 million within twelve months, mostly sports rights; 1.96x total debt and 2.67x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA; programming and production costs 36.10% of last-twelve-month revenue; earliest major rights expire with the 2027-28 season | Costs are contractual and do not fall with revenue until rights end, so revenue losses fall almost fully into EBITDA | Raises operating leverage and the sensitivity of free cash flow to revenue decline | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Versant Media Group, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway. The module synthesises the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance outputs with the four filings into one credit view, a materiality ranking and monitoring triggers. It gives no security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Versant's fundamental credit profile is adequate but weakening: low leverage and strong cash flow protect creditors today, but a shrinking pay-television core and heavy cash use on distributions and acquisitions are eroding that cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 1,876 million, or 0.88x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, and USD 1,976 million, or 0.92x, pro forma for the USD 100 million accelerated repurchase from 2026-11-04. Free cash flow of USD 1,640 million over twelve months covers the USD 120 million of annual term loan amortization many times, but nine-month distributions and acquisitions of USD 1,212 million equalled free cash flow of USD 1,210 million. The covenant definition is not supplied, so headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The strongest support is low leverage backed by cash flow that still covers debt service by a wide margin. Total debt is 1.37x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and net debt of USD 1,876 million is 0.88x, or USD 1,976 million and 0.92x pro forma for the USD 100 million accelerated repurchase from 2026-11-04; reported EBITDA covered nine-month cash interest 11.25x, and free cash flow of USD 1,640 million over twelve months converts 76.60% of EBITDA and is 56.03% of total debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The weakest dimension is revenue durability, because the two lines that earn 82.40% of revenue are in measured decline. Linear distribution fell 6.49% and advertising 3.56% in nine months 2026, after subscriber declines of 8% in each of 2024 and 2025 and a ratings decline of 17% at the networks in 2025, while platforms grew 6.43% but by only USD 40 million against a USD 201 million fall in linear distribution; issuer-stated Adjusted EBITDA fell 10.96% in nine months, and its last-twelve-month margin of 33.94% is 2.32 percentage points below FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating leverage is high because content costs are fixed and larger than the debt. Programming and production obligations of USD 5,726 million, mostly multiyear sports rights, are 1.96x total debt and 2.67x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, and programming and production costs are 36.10% of last-twelve-month revenue, so lost revenue falls almost fully into EBITDA until rights expire, the earliest being the 2027-28 season.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is the swing factor and is drawing the cushion down. In nine months 2026 distributions of USD 406 million and acquisitions and investments of USD 806 million together took 100.17% of free cash flow of USD 1,210 million, net debt rose USD 400 million in the third quarter, and the USD 2,250 million separation payment to Comcast, 75.00% of the debt principal raised, set the starting leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and refinancing are adequate and concentrated in one date. Cash plus the undrawn USD 750 million revolving facility is USD 1,801 million before the announced repurchase, for which pro forma cash is not established, and it covers the USD 120 million of annual amortization 15.01x; every instrument matures in January 2031, so refinancing depends on 2030 earnings and market access then, not on a nearer wall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99–100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The primary downside path is a faster fall in linear distribution and advertising against fixed content costs while discretionary cash use continues. If the nine-month declines repeated for twelve months with costs unchanged, reported EBITDA would fall USD 251.46 million to USD 1,889.54 million and pro forma net leverage would reach 1.05x; if the declines in linear distribution and advertising doubled, EBITDA would fall USD 558.60 million to USD 1,582.40 million, pro forma net leverage would reach 1.25x, cover on accrued interest would be 7.46x, and distributions and acquisitions at the nine-month pace would draw cash down by USD 534.60 million in a year. That is erosion of the cushion, not a liquidity event, and the first signals are linear distribution declines above 6.49% and an Adjusted EBITDA margin below 34.13%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control and governance add event risk without adding support. One Class B holder holds a third of the votes with separate approval rights, a tax matters agreement restricts equity issuance for two years after 2026-01-02 so an equity cure is not a realistic backstop, and the sponsor and governance risk level assessed in Business & governance is medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant and the asset base are the least visible parts of the credit. The maximum first lien net leverage of 3.50x is tested from the third quarter of 2026 on a definition that is not supplied, and goodwill of USD 8,127 million is 64.21% of total assets with fair value only about 11% above carrying value at the networks reporting unit, so neither covenant headroom nor impairment room is established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weakening view is the cash flow that remains. Free cash flow of USD 1,640 million over twelve months is 56.03% of total debt, revenue fell only 3.01% in nine months, the company paid USD 1,212 million of distributions and acquisitions without borrowing after January, and viewership of some networks rises in election years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the decline in linear distribution slowed toward the growth of platforms, or if buybacks and acquisitions stopped outrunning free cash flow. It would worsen if pro forma net leverage kept rising from 0.92x while EBITDA fell, if revolver borrowings funded distributions, or if the covenant's definition proved tighter than reported EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant definition and the executed credit agreements are not supplied, so the distance between current leverage and the 3.50x maximum is not measured, and the finding that leverage is low rests on reported EBITDA, which may differ from the covenant's measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No ratings, market prices, spreads or peer financials are supplied, so the adequate assessment rests on absolute ratios and cannot be set against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Last-twelve-month figures join a combined carve-out stub of 2025 to standalone 2026 months, so net leverage of 0.88x, or 0.92x pro forma for the repurchase announced for 2026-11-04, and the 76.60% cash conversion are indicative, not run-rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management guidance, forecast or subscriber data is supplied, so the downside scenarios apply nine-month 2026 rates to last-twelve-month revenue as assumptions, show the scale of exposure and say nothing about its likelihood.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The size of the advertising receivables that Comcast retained is not stated, so 2026 operating cash flow cannot be cleaned and free cash flow conversion is understated by an unknown amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The carrying value of the networks reporting unit is not stated, so the dollar cushion behind the 11% headroom, and how much of it a rise of 100 bp in the discount rate would remove, cannot be calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow covers debt service by a wide margin, which is the main support for creditors. Free cash flow of USD 1,640 million over twelve months is 56.03% of total debt and, with capital expenditures at 2.09% of revenue, most EBITDA reaches cash; scheduled amortization of USD 120 million a year is 7.32% of that free cash flow, so scheduled debt service would stay covered even if free cash flow fell sharply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and a single maturity date remove near-term refinancing risk. Cash plus the undrawn USD 750 million revolving facility is USD 1,801 million before the announced repurchase and all debt falls due in January 2031, so default risk in the next two years rests on discretionary choices, not on a maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99–100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation CALC-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Brand reach and a growing platforms line give some revenue outside cable fees. The networks reach 49 million to 60 million households each, sports rights run into the 2030s, and platforms revenue grew 6.43% to 13.44% of nine-month revenue, although management's description of audience strength is not tested against peers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is structurally declining in its two largest lines and costs do not fall with it. Linear distribution and advertising are 82.40% of revenue and fell 6.49% and 3.56%, while content obligations of USD 5,726 million are 1.96x total debt, so each lost dollar of revenue is mostly a lost dollar of EBITDA until rights expire.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is spending the cushion: distributions of USD 406 million and acquisitions and investments of USD 806 million took 100.17% of free cash flow in nine months, net debt rose USD 400 million in the third quarter, and a further USD 100 million repurchase was announced, so deleveraging is not being chosen while earnings fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dependence on Comcast and a concentrated control structure limit creditors' options. Advertising, 23.63% of nine-month revenue, is sold by NBCUniversal for approximately two years, the CNBC trademark licence has a five-year initial term, a Class B holder has a third of the votes, and equity issuance is restricted until early 2028, so there is neither a stated support provider nor a ready equity cure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Asset quality and covenant visibility are weak points. Goodwill is 64.21% of total assets, the networks reporting unit's fair value is only about 11% above carrying value, and the 3.50x first lien covenant cannot be tested because its definition is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; calculation CALC-19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Versant is a United States cable-network group built around news and sports: MS NOW, CNBC, USA Network and Golf Channel, with E!, SYFY and Oxygen True Crime, and the platforms GolfNow, Fandango, Rotten Tomatoes and, from 2026-08-03, Full Swing. Revenue comes from fees paid by cable and virtual distributors (58.76% of nine-month 2026 revenue), advertising sold by NBCUniversal under a commercial agreement for approximately two years (23.63%), transaction-based platforms (13.44%) and content licensing (4.16%). The fee base rests on distribution contracts whose terms are not disclosed and revenue is cyclical with sporting events and election years, so cash-flow visibility is moderate and falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is public and dispersed, with former Comcast shareholders holding two thirds of the votes and one Class B holder a third with approval rights; no financial sponsor is named and no equity support commitment appears. The company was carved out of Comcast on 2026-01-02 with USD 3,000 million of secured debt, of which USD 2,250 million went to Comcast, and its ties to Comcast continue through advertising sales, transition services, a trademark licence and a tax matters agreement. Creditors therefore face the board's own policy on leverage, shareholder returns and acquisitions, and no source states sponsor-style support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is largely recurring but structurally declining. Linear distribution is a per-subscriber fee, so volume follows distributor subscribers, which fell 8% in each of 2024 and 2025, while price rises under contracts only partly offset the loss; the ten largest distributors were 52% of receivables at 2026-09-30, so a few renewals decide pricing power, and the separation ended joint negotiation with NBCUniversal's broadcast networks. Advertising is priced on ratings, which declined 17% in 2025, and platforms revenue follows box office and golf rounds, so revenue is predictable in its core, discretionary and cyclical at the edges, and declining in the two largest lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended only partly. Programming and production costs of USD 1,777 million for nine months, mainly licensed content and sports rights, are contractual and fall with revenue only as rights end, other costs rise with platform volumes, and standalone costs replace the allocations Comcast charged before 2026, with fees to NBCUniversal for advertising sales added to selling costs. Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 34.13% from 37.18% and operating income margin to 18.66% from 21.13% as revenue fell 3.01% and total costs stayed flat, so volume pressure and operating deleverage are the exposures and cost cuts depend on content decisions at renewal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business needs little capital, so most EBITDA reaches cash. Capital expenditures were USD 103 million for nine months, 2.09% of revenue, cash interest and taxes paid were USD 415 million, and free cash flow converted 76.60% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA before USD 1,212 million of distributions and acquisitions. Operating cash flow of USD 1,313 million against USD 1,546 million a year earlier is understated because Comcast kept advertising receivables at the separation, and low capital needs leave little to cut, so the flexible uses of cash are buybacks, acquisitions and dividends, not investment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-21; calculation CALC-08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense: the networks compete for distribution, advertising and programming with other networks, streaming services and social platforms, and the filings call sports programming significantly more competitive and expensive, so rights cost inflation meets falling ratings and compresses margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is modest for networks, where rights and audience scale are barriers, and higher for platforms, where Fandango and GolfNow face competing ticketing and booking applications, so platforms growth is less protected than the networks' fee base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes is high: streaming and direct-to-consumer services pull subscribers out of cable bundles, which is why subscribers fell 8% a year in 2024 and 2025 and why advertising ratings fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high: the ten largest distributors were 52% of receivables, distributors may tier or drop networks as their own subscribers fall, advertisers buy on ratings, and the loss of joint negotiation with NBCUniversal weakens renewals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is high: sports leagues and rights holders set multiyear prices that are fixed obligations of USD 5,726 million, with renewals from the 2027-28 season, and NBCUniversal supplies advertising sales and services under agreements that end in about two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Social and technological change is the material external factor, because consumers moving to streaming and digital video reduce subscribers and ratings, which drives both fee and advertising revenue. Economic factors matter through rates and spending: a rise of 100 bp in the discount rate would cut the networks reporting unit's fair value by about USD 660 million, a change of 100 bp in floating rates moves interest expense by about USD 8 million over nine months, and platforms and advertising follow consumer spending. Political and regulatory factors, including program access rules that could limit exclusive contracts with Comcast and privacy and consumer-protection rules, are not a primary credit driver on the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths that support credit are low leverage, free cash flow that covers amortization many times, a single 2031 maturity with USD 1,801 million of liquidity before the announced repurchase, and sports and news brands with rights into the 2030s.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-04; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses that constrain credit are the decline in linear distribution and advertising, fixed content obligations of USD 5,726 million, a cash-heavy financial policy, dependence on Comcast contracts and a thin goodwill cushion at the networks reporting unit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit are platforms growth beyond 13.44% of revenue, election-year viewership, management's plan to extend the networks to ad-supported and subscription streaming and over-the-air distribution, and the choice to pay down debt from surplus cash instead of repurchasing stock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation CALC-01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken credit are faster subscriber loss, renewals with distributors on worse terms after the separation, rights inflation from the 2027-28 season, the end of NBCUniversal's advertising sales and transition services around early 2028, and a goodwill impairment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are low leverage, strong cash conversion, ample near-term liquidity and a single maturity in January 2031. The main constraints are a declining revenue core against fixed content commitments, a financial policy that spends free cash flow on distributions and acquisitions, dependence on Comcast arrangements, concentrated control with restricted equity issuance, and an unverified covenant. The trend is negative on earnings, with nine-month Adjusted EBITDA down 10.96% and margin down, and neutral on leverage, where net debt rose USD 400 million in the third quarter. The datapoints that would settle the view are the covenant definition and executed agreements, subscriber and renewal data, the amount of retained receivables, and ratings and market data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the likely path is continued revenue decline in linear distribution and advertising, margin pressure as costs stay fixed, free cash flow still well above amortization, and net debt drifting up if distributions and acquisitions continue, with the announced repurchase adding USD 100 million. Tailwinds are platforms growth and election-year viewership; headwinds are subscriber losses, ratings declines and the cost of replacing Comcast services as the transition services end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_vsnt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the events that matter are the end of the tax matters restrictions, transition services and NBCUniversal advertising sales around early 2028, the renewal of the Premier League rights from the 2027-28 season and other major rights through 2033, the end of the CNBC trademark licence's initial term in 2031, and the January 2031 maturity of all debt. Each is a point at which revenue, cost or funding terms reset, so the 2031 refinancing will be judged on earnings after the rights renewals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a faster loss of cable subscribers and lower ratings, for example at a major distributor renewal made without NBCUniversal's joint negotiating weight. The first operational break is linear distribution and advertising revenue falling faster than the 6.49% and 3.56% seen in nine months 2026, while content obligations of USD 5,726 million do not fall. In the first scenario, with the nine-month declines repeated for twelve months and platforms growing at 6.43%, revenue and EBITDA fall USD 251.46 million, pro forma net leverage rises to 1.05x and interest cover on accrued interest stays at 8.91x. In the second scenario, with the declines doubled, EBITDA falls USD 558.60 million, pro forma net leverage rises to 1.25x, and discretionary uses at the nine-month pace exceed free cash flow by USD 534.60 million a year, leaving cash of USD 516.40 million after one year, from a base of USD 1,051 million before the announced repurchase, before any revolver draw.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation CALC-12; calculation CALC-13; calculation CALC-14; calculation CALC-15; calculation CALC-16; calculation CALC-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has levers: the USD 700 million of remaining repurchase authorisation and the announced USD 100 million repurchase are discretionary, acquisitions can stop, the dividend of about USD 205.04 million a year is 12.50% of free cash flow, and the USD 750 million revolving facility is undrawn, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress on these assumptions. The scenarios are assumptions without tax effects or cost actions and do not test the first lien covenant, whose definition is not supplied. Primary downside path: linear distribution and advertising cash flow eroding against fixed content commitments while buybacks and acquisitions continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_vsnt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation CALC-17; calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Versant presents an adequate business profile supported by national news and sports brands reaching 49 million to 60 million households and a growing platforms line, but credit quality is constrained by structural decline in linear distribution and advertising, fixed content commitments of USD 5,726 million and a cash-heavy financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate for debt service and weak against discretionary uses, because free cash flow of USD 1,640 million covers amortization many times while distributions and acquisitions took 100.17% of free cash flow in nine months. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on 2030 earnings, the outcome of sports rights renewals through 2033 and capital market access, as all debt matures in January 2031. The primary downside path is a faster fall in linear distribution and advertising against fixed content costs while buybacks and acquisitions continue. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreements and covenant definition, subscriber and renewal data, the 2026 proxy statement, and ratings and market data. Top risk: erosion of linear distribution and advertising cash flow against fixed content commitments.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-10; calculation CALC-01
